Employment, compensation, privacy, legal, tax, and regulatory matters must be confirmed in the relevant signed agreement and reviewed by qualified professionals where necessary. Handbook purpose This handbook turns Engage Lynk’s strategy into repeatable actions. It explains what the company stands for, how the team communicates, how prospects are researched and engaged, how meetings are run, how campaigns are measured, and how company information is protected. Who should use it  Founders and leadership  Business-development representatives  Sales and appointment-setting team members  Marketing and campaign specialists  Operations and reporting staff  Employees, trainees, and approved contractors Document hierarchy Priorit y Document Purpose 1 Signed agreement Controls role, compensation, term, confidentiality, and binding conditions. 2 Approved client scope Controls deliverables, targets, timelines, and client-specific expectations. 3 Company policy or SOP Controls recurring internal processes. 4 This handbook Provides the standard operating framework and training guidance.

chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | ULTIMATE HANDBOOK Internal Use | Engage Lynk | 5 CHAPTER 02 Company Identity A clear understanding of who Engage Lynk is, what it offers, and how it should be described. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Company profile Engage Lynk is a B2B growth and outreach company based in Zirakpur, Punjab. Its operating focus includes targeted campaigns, high-value outreach, lead generation, business development, marketing support, and transparent reporting. Client engagements should be designed around the client’s market, offer, target accounts, and commercial goals. chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | ULTIMATE HANDBOOK Internal Use | Engage Lynk | 6 CHAPTER 03 Mission, Vision, and Principles The beliefs that guide decisions even when no manager is present. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Mission Create meaningful commercial connections through intelligent targeting, disciplined outreach, and measurable execution. chunks.title: Ultimate Handbook
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | ULTIMATE HANDBOOK Internal Use | Engage Lynk | 11 CHAPTER 08 Professional Conduct Standards for respectful, reliable, and safe representation of the company. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Expected conduct  Be truthful about capabilities, experience, results, and timelines.  Do not make discriminatory, threatening, humiliating, or inappropriate remarks.  Do not pressure prospects who clearly decline.  Do not use company assets for unauthorized personal activity.  Do not speak on behalf of a client without authorization.  Do not offer discounts, guarantees, or contract terms without approval. Conflicts and gifts Any financial interest, outside relationship, competing work, referral payment, or gift that could influence company decisions should be disclosed to management before action is taken. Escalation standard If conduct appears unsafe, illegal, misleading, or materially harmful, stop the activity and escalate it immediately. Do not attempt to conceal or complete the action.

chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | ULTIMATE HANDBOOK Internal Use | Engage Lynk | 14 CHAPTER 11 Prospect Research SOP A repeatable process for producing informed conversations instead of generic outreach. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Research checklist  Company website and primary offer☐  Industry and target customer☐  Geographic market☐  Prospect name, role, and likely responsibilities☐  Recent company initiative or relevant trigger☐  Current sales or marketing motion if visible☐  Possible challenge or opportunity☐  Approved reason for contact☐  Personalization line☐  Source links and research date☐ Research output Field Example format Observation Company is expanding its enterprise offering. Hypothesis Sales team may need additional decision-maker access. Relevant service Account research plus multichannel appointment setting. Discovery question How are you currently building enterprise pipeline? Next action Call prospect and send tailored introduction. Quality rule Research supports a hypothesis, not a conclusion. Ask the prospect to confirm the real situation before offering a solution.

chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | ULTIMATE HANDBOOK Internal Use | Engage Lynk | 16 CHAPTER 13 Cold Calling Playbook The standard system for reaching operators, decision-makers, and busy executives. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Operator opening “Hello, may I please speak with [Prospect Name]?” If asked for context: “I’m [Name] from Engage Lynk. I’m calling regarding a potential business- development discussion with [Prospect Name].” Prospect opening “Hi [Prospect Name], this is [Name] from Engage Lynk. I’m glad I could connect with you. Have I reached you at an acceptable time for a brief introduction?” “Engage Lynk supports B2B companies with targeted outreach, lead generation, marketing, and business development. May I ask one quick question about your current growth process?” Discovery options  Are you satisfied with the number and quality of opportunities entering your pipeline?  Which customer segment is most important for your growth this year?  Is your sales team spending more time prospecting or closing?  Are there any markets or services you want to expand? Meeting ask “Rather than give you a generic pitch, we would like to understand your business and prepare a customized approach. Would you be available for a focused 20-minute discussion this week or next?”

chunks.title: Ultimate Handbook
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | ULTIMATE HANDBOOK Internal Use | Engage Lynk | 17 CHAPTER 14 Gatekeeper and Objection Handling Respectful responses that preserve credibility and create a clear next step. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Situation Recommended response Send information “Certainly. Which area is most relevant: lead generation, sales development, marketing, or market expansion?” Already have an agency “Understood. We can focus the discussion on whether there is an uncovered segment, market, or pipeline gap.” Not interested “I understand. Is that because the current pipeline is sufficient, or because this is not a current priority?” Busy “Of course. Would another time be suitable, or may I email a brief introduction and follow up later?” No budget “Understood. Is the priority itself relevant if the commercial model can be reviewed later?” Doing well “That is good to hear. The discussion may still be useful if expansion or additional ROI is a priority.” Boundary rule One clarification is acceptable. Repeated pressure after a clear refusal is not.

chunks.title: Ultimate Handbook
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | ULTIMATE HANDBOOK Internal Use | Engage Lynk | 18 CHAPTER 15 Email Outreach Playbook Short, relevant emails that support a coordinated conversation. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Subject-line standard When emailing a client or prospect, include the client or prospect’s first name and company name in the subject whenever appropriate. Initial email Subject: [First Name] | [Company Name] growth discussion Hi [First Name], I noticed [relevant business observation]. Engage Lynk helps B2B companies build qualified pipeline through targeted outreach, marketing support, and business development. I would like to understand whether [specific objective] is currently a priority for [Company Name]. Would a focused 20-minute discussion next week be useful? Regards, [Name] | Engage Lynk Follow-up email Subject: [First Name] | [Company Name] next step Hi [First Name], I am following up on the business-development opportunity discussed. Based on our initial view, there may be scope to support [objective]. If this remains relevant, I can arrange a focused discussion and prepare a customized plan around your target market and sales process. Regards, [Name] | Engage Lynk Email checklist  One clear reason for contact☐  One relevant observation☐  One primary call to action☐  No unsupported results or guarantees☐  Correct name and company☐  Professional signature☐  Tracker updated after sending☐

chunks.title: Ultimate Handbook
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | ULTIMATE HANDBOOK Internal Use | Engage Lynk | 19 CHAPTER 16 LinkedIn and Social Selling Use professional familiarity and relevance, not repetitive pitching. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Connection request Connection note “Hi [First Name], I have been reviewing [Company Name] in relation to its work in [sector]. I would be glad to connect.” After acceptance Conversation opener “Thank you for connecting. I noticed [specific observation]. Engage Lynk supports B2B companies with targeted outreach and business development. Is [relevant objective] currently part of your growth plan?” Social-selling rules  Do not copy the same long pitch into every message.  Do not send multiple channels on the same day without coordination.  Use public information responsibly and accurately.  Stop automated or scheduled touches when a prospect replies.  Move substantive commercial discussions into a meeting or approved channel.

chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | ULTIMATE HANDBOOK Internal Use | Engage Lynk | 20 CHAPTER 17 Multichannel Sequence A coordinated sequence in which each contact builds on the previous one. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Day Channel Purpose Action 1 Email Establish relevance Personalized introduction 2 LinkedIn Create recognition Connection request 4 Phone Start conversation Reference the business reason 7 Email Add value Share concise insight or proposed angle 10 Phone Qualify priority Ask focused discovery question 14 LinkedIn or email Close loop Request meeting or pause outreach Sequence principle The channels should feel like one coherent conversation. chunks.title: Ultimate Handbook
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | ULTIMATE HANDBOOK Internal Use | Engage Lynk | 21 CHAPTER 18 Discovery Meeting Playbook A prospect-first meeting that gathers evidence before Engage Lynk proposes a customized plan. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Recommended 20-minute agenda Time Stage Objective 0–3 min Introductions Establish roles and purpose 3–10 min Business understanding Learn offer, customers, market, and sales process 10–15 min Goals and challenges Define desired outcomes and constraints 15–18 min Engage Lynk fit Explain relevant capabilities briefly 18–20 min Next step Agree customized plan, owner, and date Core questions  Could you briefly introduce your business and your role?  Who are your primary customers?  Which markets or segments are you targeting?  How do you currently generate new business?  What is the biggest obstacle in the current sales process?  What does a qualified opportunity look like?  What result would make a 90-day campaign valuable?  Who should be involved in reviewing the customized plan? Transition to customized plan “Thank you. That gives us a clearer understanding of your business. Based on what you have shared, we will prepare a customized plan covering the target market, ideal customer profile, outreach channels, qualification process, reporting, timeline, and commercial model.”

chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 2 LYNK 00 Policy Status and Use How these rules connect with agreements, client instructions, and applicable law. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Legal review required This is an internal policy draft, not legal advice. chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 3 LYNK 01 The Integrity Lynk Truth before persuasion. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Every representation made in Engage Lynk’s name must be accurate, supportable, and authorized. Rules of engagement  Never fabricate clients, results, case studies, appointments, pipeline, credentials, or testimonials.  Separate fact, estimate, hypothesis, and recommendation clearly.  Correct material errors promptly and notify affected owners.  Do not conceal failed activity, complaints, missed commitments, or data incidents.  Do not sign, accept, or alter binding terms without authority.

chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 4 LYNK 02 The Respect Lynk Professional conduct in every interaction. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Engage Lynk requires respectful treatment across the workplace and in all external communication. Rules of engagement  No bullying, intimidation, humiliation, discriminatory conduct, retaliation, or abusive language.  Do not continue sales pressure after a clear refusal.  Respect names, roles, time zones, communication preferences, and accessibility needs.  Disagreements must focus on facts, decisions, and next actions.  Escalate threats, harassment, or unsafe behaviour immediately.

chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 5 LYNK 03 The Workplace Safety Lynk A workplace free from harassment and avoidable harm. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Engage Lynk is committed to a safe and dignified workplace. Rules of engagement  Sexual harassment and unwelcome sexual conduct are prohibited.  Complaints must be handled confidentially, sensitively, and without retaliation.  Management must establish the legally required complaint mechanism and committee where applicable.  Remote work, client sites, travel, calls, messages, and work events are treated as workplace contexts where applicable.  Immediate safety concerns must be escalated without delay.

chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 6 LYNK 04 The Equal Opportunity Lynk Fair access to work and development. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Employment decisions should be based on lawful, job-relevant criteria and documented performance. Rules of engagement  Do not discriminate in recruitment, assignments, training, evaluation, compensation, or progression.  Use role requirements and evidence, not stereotypes or personal bias.  Provide reasonable clarity on expectations and performance concerns.  Avoid gendered or exclusionary job advertisements unless legally justified.  Report conflicts of interest in hiring or evaluation.

chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 7 LYNK 05 The Role and Authority Lynk Know what you own and what requires approval. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Every team member must operate within the authority of their role. Rules of engagement  Confirm reporting manager, scope, target market, tools, and approval limits at onboarding.  Do not offer pricing, discounts, guarantees, legal terms, or service commitments without authority.  Escalate questions outside your scope instead of guessing.  Document delegated authority for high-impact actions.  Handoffs must identify the new owner and date.

chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 8 LYNK 06 The Time and Attendance Lynk Reliability creates trust. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Team members must honor agreed schedules, meetings, reporting times, and availability expectations. Rules of engagement  Notify the reporting manager promptly when delay or absence affects work.  Join client and internal meetings prepared and on time.  Record attendance or working time only through approved methods where required.  Do not misstate work completed or time spent.  Leave, holidays, and schedule changes require the agreed approval process.

chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 9 LYNK 07 The Performance Lynk Measure quality, movement, and discipline. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Performance should reflect preparation, activity, quality, conversion, policy compliance, and development. Rules of engagement  Targets must be documented and reasonably connected to the role.  Raw call or email volume is not the only performance measure.  Managers should provide specific evidence and improvement actions.  Team members must maintain accurate activity records.  Performance reviews must not be falsified or retaliatory.

chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 10 LYNK 08 The Prospect Research Lynk Research before outreach. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Senior prospects should receive relevant outreach based on a reasonable business hypothesis. Rules of engagement  Confirm company, industry, prospect role, target market, and reason for contact.  Do not present public information as confidential knowledge.  Treat inferred pain points as questions, not facts.  Record research sources and date where practical.  Avoid collecting unnecessary sensitive personal information.

chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 11 LYNK 09 The Data Sourcing Lynk Use data responsibly and traceably. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Prospect and client data may be acquired and used only for approved, legitimate business activity. Rules of engagement  Use approved providers, client lists, public sources, and authorized systems.  Record data source where practical.  Do not knowingly buy, scrape, or import prohibited or unlawfully obtained data.  Remove duplicates and obvious errors before launch.  Limit fields to what is relevant for the business purpose.

chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 12 LYNK 10 The Calling Lynk Clear identity, legitimate purpose, respectful boundaries. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Business calls must be relevant, professional, and conducted through approved resources. Rules of engagement  Identify yourself and Engage Lynk accurately.  Use approved scripts as guidance, not as permission to mislead.  Honor customer preferences, opt-outs, and applicable commercial-communication requirements.  Do not spoof caller identity or create false urgency.  Record outcomes, requirements, objections, and next actions promptly.

chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 13 LYNK 11 The Email Lynk Relevant, traceable, and controlled email communication. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Company email must support an approved business purpose and preserve professional trust. Rules of engagement  Use company accounts for company work unless an exception is approved.  Include the prospect or client first name and company name in the subject where appropriate.  Use accurate sender identity and a clear call to action.  Do not send unsupported claims, deceptive subjects, or unauthorized attachments.  Stop or suppress outreach when the recipient opts out.  Check recipients carefully before sending confidential material.

chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 14 LYNK 12 The Social Media Lynk Professional presence without unauthorized representation. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Social channels may be used for approved outreach, brand building, and recruitment with care. Rules of engagement  Do not imply official authorization beyond your role.  Do not disclose confidential information or client identities without permission.  Do not copy identical pitches across multiple channels without coordination.  Distinguish personal opinions from company statements.  Escalate public complaints or reputational risks; do not argue publicly.

chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 15 LYNK 13 The Meeting Lynk Every meeting must have a purpose, owner, and next action. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Internal and external meetings should respect time and produce usable decisions. Rules of engagement  Share or state the meeting objective.  Let prospects explain their business before presenting a solution.  Do not record meetings without required notice and approval.  Capture decisions, owners, deadlines, and follow-up questions.  Send calendar details accurately and promptly.  Do not list participants who have not agreed to attend.

chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 16 LYNK 14 The Client Lynk Serve the contracted objective, not assumptions. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Client work must follow the signed scope, approved instructions, and responsible professional judgment. Rules of engagement  Confirm deliverables, exclusions, dependencies, owners, and reporting cadence.  Do not expand material scope without written approval.  Raise delays, risks, weak data, and client dependencies early.  Protect client brand, systems, and confidential information.  Do not contact a client’s market beyond the approved campaign.

chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 17 LYNK 15 The Proposal and Pricing Lynk Commercial clarity before commitment. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Proposals and pricing must be accurate, approved, and unambiguous. Rules of engagement  State deliverables, assumptions, exclusions, timeline, payment terms, and next step.  Define success, attribution, and commission triggers in writing.  Do not promise guaranteed leads, revenue, or outcomes without authorized contractual language.  Discounts and exceptions require approval.  Use the latest approved version and preserve revision history.

chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 18 LYNK 16 The Commission Lynk Transparent attribution and payment rules. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Commission arrangements must be governed by a signed agreement and verifiable records. Rules of engagement  Define the qualifying lead, conversion event, revenue base, payment event, and protection period.  Clarify treatment of taxes, refunds, cancellations, discounts, and shared ownership.  No self-assignment or manipulation of lead ownership.  Record source, owner, and material activity in the approved tracker.  Disputes must be escalated with evidence.

chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 19 LYNK 17 The Marketing Claims Lynk Evidence before advertising. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Marketing content must be truthful, supportable, and consistent with approved positioning. Rules of engagement  Do not publish invented statistics, guarantees, testimonials, certifications, or client results.  Obtain permission before naming a client or using its logo.  Label assumptions, projections, and illustrative scenarios.  Review regulated-industry claims before publication.  Correct misleading content promptly.

chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 20 LYNK 18 The Brand Lynk One recognizable identity across every touchpoint. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Engage Lynk’s brand should consistently use its approved cyan, white, and black identity and professional voice. Rules of engagement  Use approved logos, colours, templates, and contact details.  Keep communication confident, direct, and respectful.  Do not create unofficial sub-brands or modify the logo without approval.  Check spelling, formatting, and visual readability.  Archive final approved brand assets in the approved location.

chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 21 LYNK 19 The Technology Lynk Secure use of accounts, devices, and platforms. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Company technology must be used only for authorized, secure business activities. Rules of engagement  Use assigned accounts and strong authentication.  Do not share passwords, one-time codes, API keys, or licensed seats.  Install software or browser extensions only when approved.  Lock devices and keep operating systems reasonably updated.  Report suspicious logins, malware, or account compromise immediately.

chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 22 LYNK 20 The Google Workspace Lynk Controlled collaboration and file ownership. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Company email, calendars, drives, and documents must remain organized, accessible, and protected. Rules of engagement  Use shared company locations for operational files.  Assign appropriate sharing permissions and review external access.  Do not transfer files to personal accounts.  Use clear file names and version control.  Remove access promptly when roles or projects end.

chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 23 LYNK 21 The Apollo.io Lynk Responsible prospecting through licensed access. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Apollo.io access is for approved prospect research and campaigns only. Rules of engagement  Do not share accounts or export data for personal use.  Follow approved ICP filters and campaign ownership.  Avoid duplicate enrollment and conflicting sequences.  Stop automation when a prospect replies or opts out.  Record material outcomes in the company tracker.

chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 24 LYNK 22 The SIM and Calling Resource Lynk Company communication assets remain company property. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Company-issued SIM cards, numbers, and devices may be used only for approved business activity. Rules of engagement  Do not use company calling resources for unauthorized personal or third-party work.  Protect PINs, devices, call records, and associated accounts.  Report loss, theft, damage, or misuse immediately.  Return the resource when requested or when engagement ends.  Do not port, transfer, or register the resource elsewhere without approval.

chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 25 LYNK 23 The Excel and CRM Lynk If it is not recorded, it is not controlled. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Lead and opportunity records must be timely, factual, standardized, and complete. Rules of engagement  Use approved stage names and one accountable owner.  Every active record requires a next action and date.  Do not delete, backdate, inflate, or conceal records.  Keep notes factual, professional, and relevant.  Separate scheduled meetings, attended meetings, opportunities, won revenue, and collected revenue.

chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 26 LYNK 24 The Confidentiality Lynk Information is shared by need, not curiosity. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Non-public company, client, prospect, employee, and partner information must be protected. Rules of engagement  Use confidential information only for the approved purpose.  Share only with authorized people who need it.  Do not discuss confidential matters in public or uncontrolled channels.  Do not forward files to personal email or storage.  Return or delete information when instructed and legally permitted.  Confidentiality continues after the engagement ends as provided in the signed agreement.

chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 27 LYNK 25 The Privacy Lynk Purpose, minimization, accuracy, security, and respect. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Personal data must be handled for lawful, approved purposes with appropriate safeguards. chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 28 LYNK 26 The AI Lynk Human accountability for AI-assisted work. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement AI may assist research, drafting, analysis, and productivity, but authorized people remain responsible for outputs. chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 29 LYNK 27 The Records Lynk Preserve evidence without retaining everything forever. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Company records must be stored, retained, and disposed of according to approved business, contractual, and legal needs. chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 30 LYNK 28 The Expense Lynk Company money requires prior purpose and evidence. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Expenses must be necessary, reasonable, authorized, and supported by valid records. chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 31 LYNK 29 The Conflict of Interest Lynk Disclose interests before they influence decisions. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Personal interests must not improperly influence company, client, hiring, vendor, or sales decisions. Rules of engagement  Disclose competing work, financial interests, referral fees, close personal interests, and vendor relationships.  Do not use company opportunities or confidential information for personal gain.  Do not accept gifts or benefits that may influence judgment.  Recuse yourself where directed.  Keep conflict decisions documented.

chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 32 LYNK 30 The Incident Lynk Stop, preserve, report, contain, learn. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Material security, privacy, conduct, client, financial, or reputational incidents require immediate escalation. Rules of engagement  Stop the affected activity when safe and practical.  Preserve factual evidence and do not alter records.  Notify the designated manager or incident owner promptly.  Do not make unauthorized public statements or admissions.  Follow containment and communication instructions.  Record corrective and preventive actions.

chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 33 LYNK 31 The Complaint and Whistleblowing Lynk Concerns may be raised without retaliation. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Engage Lynk should provide confidential channels for good-faith concerns about misconduct, safety, harassment, fraud, privacy, or legal compliance. Rules of engagement  Raise concerns with the manager or designated complaint channel.  Managers must not suppress or retaliate against good-faith reports.  Confidentiality should be protected to the extent reasonably possible.  Investigations must be impartial, documented, and need-to-know.  Knowingly false allegations may be addressed through a fair process.

chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 34 LYNK 32 The Disciplinary Lynk Fair, documented, and proportionate correction. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement Policy concerns should be assessed consistently, with attention to evidence, severity, repetition, intent, and impact. Rules of engagement  Provide notice of the concern and a reasonable opportunity to respond, subject to urgent safety or access controls.  Use coaching or corrective action for minor issues where appropriate.  Serious misconduct may justify immediate restriction or termination subject to agreement and law.  Document decisions and protect confidentiality.  Do not retaliate against protected complaints or cooperation.

chunks.title: Rules of Engagement
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | RULES OF ENGAGEMENT Internal Policy Manual | Engage Lynk | 35 LYNK 33 The Offboarding Lynk Close every access, asset, and responsibility loop. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Policy statement The end of an engagement must protect business continuity and confidential information. chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | BD PARTNERS SOP Internal Use | Engage Lynk | 11 SECTION 09 Calling Procedure Use clear identity, permission, relevance, discovery, and a controlled meeting ask. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Operator opening “Hello, may I please speak with [Prospect Name]?” If context is requested: “I’m [Name], an authorized business-development partner with Engage Lynk. I’m calling regarding a potential business-growth discussion with [Prospect Name].” Prospect opening “Hi [Prospect Name], this is [Name], an authorized business-development partner with Engage Lynk. I’m glad I could connect with you. Have I reached you at an acceptable time for a brief introduction?” “Engage Lynk supports B2B companies with targeted outreach, lead generation, marketing support, and business development. May I ask one quick question about your current growth process?” Discovery options  Which customer segment is most important to your growth right now?  Are you satisfied with the quality and consistency of opportunities entering the pipeline?  Is your team spending more time prospecting or closing?  Are you entering a new market, geography, or service category? Meeting ask “Rather than give you a generic pitch, the next step would be a focused discussion to understand your business and determine whether a customized plan is appropriate. Would you be available for 20 minutes this week or next?” After-call procedure 8. Record disposition immediately. 9. Capture prospect language, not an embellished interpretation. 10.Confirm any promised email or calendar action. 11.Set a specific next action and date. 12.Stop future automated touches when the prospect replies or opts out.

chunks.title: BD Partners SOP
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | BD PARTNERS SOP Internal Use | Engage Lynk | 12 SECTION 10 Email and LinkedIn Procedure Partner communication must be personalized, accurate, and attributable. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Initial email Subject: [First Name] | [Company Name] growth discussion Hi [First Name], I noticed [relevant observation]. I am an authorized business-development partner with Engage Lynk. Engage Lynk supports B2B companies through targeted outreach, lead generation, marketing support, and business development. Would a focused 20-minute discussion be useful to understand whether [specific objective] is currently a priority for [Company Name]? Regards, [Name] | BD Partner, Engage Lynk LinkedIn connection “Hi [First Name], I have been reviewing [Company Name] in relation to [sector or objective]. I work with Engage Lynk on B2B growth opportunities and would be glad to connect.” Communication rules  Use approved identity and signature.  Do not imply employment if the relationship is contractual or independent.  Do not use deceptive subject lines or unsupported proof.  Do not attach confidential proposals or pricing without approval.  Honor opt-outs and suppress further outreach.  Record material communication in the tracker.

chunks.title: BD Partners SOP
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | BD PARTNERS SOP Internal Use | Engage Lynk | 13 SECTION 11 Qualification Framework Promote relevance and readiness, not inflated lead counts. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Qualification dimensions Dimension Evidence to capture Fit Industry, geography, company profile, and approved service relevance Need Problem, goal, gap, or opportunity acknowledged by the prospect Authority Decision-maker, influencer, evaluator, or referral path Timing Current priority, planned period, or nurture date Commercial context Budget information if voluntarily discussed; do not pressure Next step Meeting, information request, internal review, proposal, or nurture Qualified opportunity minimum  Prospect identity and company are verified.  A relevant business need or goal is recorded.  The Engage Lynk service fit is plausible and approved.  The prospect has agreed to a defined next step or requested relevant information.  Notes, owner, date, and supporting evidence are complete. Quality standard A positive response without fit or a business next step is engagement, not necessarily a qualified opportunity.

chunks.title: BD Partners SOP
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | BD PARTNERS SOP Internal Use | Engage Lynk | 14 SECTION 12 Discovery Meeting Procedure Understand the business first, then explain the customized-plan process. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Time Stage BD Partner action 0–3 min Introductions Clarify role, meeting purpose, and attendees. 3–10 min Business understanding Invite the prospect to explain company, customers, market, and current process. 10–15 min Goals and challenges Explore priority, need, decision process, and success criteria. 15–18 min Engage Lynk relevance Explain only the capabilities relevant to what was shared. 18–20 min Next step Agree customized plan, decision participants, owner, and date. Mandatory questions  Could you briefly introduce the business and your role?  Who are your primary customers?  Which markets or customer segments are you prioritizing?  How do you currently generate new opportunities?  What is the biggest constraint in the current process?  What would make a 90-day engagement valuable?  Who should review a customized plan and commercial proposal? Transition statement “Thank you. Based on what you have shared, Engage Lynk can prepare a customized plan covering target accounts, buyer roles, channels, qualification, reporting, timeline, responsibilities, and commercial structure.”

chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | BD PARTNERS SOP Internal Use | Engage Lynk | 15 SECTION 13 Meeting Handoff to Engage Lynk Transfer context without forcing the prospect to repeat the entire conversation. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Handoff pack Field Required detail Prospect and company Complete before acceptance Meeting date and attendees Complete before acceptance Relationship source Complete before acceptance Business overview Complete before acceptance Need and goals Complete before acceptance Current process Complete before acceptance Priority and timing Complete before acceptance Authority and decision path Complete before acceptance Objections or sensitivities Complete before acceptance Requested topics Complete before acceptance Relevant links and evidence Complete before acceptance Agreed next action Complete before acceptance Acceptance procedure 13.BD Partner submits the handoff before the agreed internal cutoff. 14.Engage Lynk owner reviews fit, completeness, conflict, and meeting readiness. 15.Missing information is returned for correction. 16.Accepted opportunity receives an Engage Lynk owner and stage. 17.Calendar, presentation preparation, and follow-up ownership are confirmed.

chunks.title: BD Partners SOP
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | BD PARTNERS SOP Internal Use | Engage Lynk | 16 SECTION 14 Proposal, Pricing, and Negotiation Boundaries Protect commercial clarity and prevent unauthorized promises. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ BD Partner may  Provide verified prospect context.  Explain approved service categories at a high level.  Collect questions, priorities, and commercial concerns.  Coordinate the proposal meeting.  Support relationship continuity during negotiation. BD Partner may not without written authorization  Issue final pricing or discounts.  Change scope, timelines, payment terms, or commission rules.  Guarantee meetings, leads, conversion, revenue, or ROI.  Sign contracts or accept legal terms.  Commit delivery resources or employee assignments.  Use unapproved case studies, certifications, or client names. Escalation phrase “I want to make sure I give you an accurate and authorized answer. I will take this back to the Engage Lynk commercial team and confirm it in writing.”

chunks.title: BD Partners SOP
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | BD PARTNERS SOP Internal Use | Engage Lynk | 17 SECTION 15 Opportunity Attribution and Commission Commission follows documented rules, not memory or informal claims. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Attribution evidence  Accepted account registration  Source and relationship evidence  Meaningful activity history  Qualification notes  Meeting and handoff records  Signed commercial outcome or collected revenue as required  No unresolved duplicate, exclusion, conflict, or policy breach Commission workflow 18.Partner registers the opportunity before or immediately after the first authorized contact. 19.BD operations validates ownership and exclusions. 20.Partner develops and records the opportunity. 21.Engage Lynk records the qualifying conversion event. 22.Finance or management validates the commission base after the contractual payment trigger. 23.Commission statement is issued or recorded under the agreed cadence. 24.Disputes are raised within the agreement’s stated period with evidence. Issue Treatment must be defined in agreement Shared opportunity Split, primary owner, or management allocation Existing account Exclusion or approved expansion credit Refund or cancellation Clawback or no-payment rule Discount Commission on gross, net, or collected amount Taxes and pass-through costs Included or excluded from commission base Late payment or bad debt Payment only after collection, if agreed Termination Protection period and eligible pipeline

chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | BD PARTNERS SOP Internal Use | Engage Lynk | 18 SECTION 16 Daily, Weekly, and Monthly Operating Rhythm Consistent follow-through prevents partner programs from becoming invisible pipelines. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Cadence BD Partner Engage Lynk owner Daily Review replies, research priorities, execute approved touches, update records Handle urgent escalations and active handoffs Weekly Submit pipeline, meetings, objections, risks, and next actions Review quality, ownership, conversion, and coaching Monthly Review territory performance, stale accounts, forecast, and learning Confirm strategy, attribution, enablement, and continuation Quarterly Business review and development plan Renew, expand, correct, pause, or exit partnership Weekly review agenda  Wins and material changes  New registered accounts  Qualified opportunities  Meetings scheduled and attended  Stalled or disputed accounts  Top objections and market feedback  Data and compliance issues  Support required  Owners and due dates

chunks.title: BD Partners SOP
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | BD PARTNERS SOP Internal Use | Engage Lynk | 19 SECTION 17 KPIs and Quality Scorecard Use a balanced scorecard that protects quality and commercial value. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Dimension Example indicators Coverage Approved accounts researched and activated Engagement Decision-maker connects and meaningful replies Qualification Accepted opportunities and rejection reasons Meetings Scheduled, attended, and accepted by Engage Lynk Pipeline Stage movement and evidence-based value Commercial Closed and collected revenue under agreed attribution Quality ICP fit, notes, attendance, duplicate rate, complaint rate Discipline Timely updates, policy compliance, training completion Metric rule Targets must be documented by campaign or territory. This SOP intentionally does not invent universal daily quotas because appropriate volume depends on market, channel, data quality, relationship model, and approved campaign design.

chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | BD PARTNERS SOP Internal Use | Engage Lynk | 20 SECTION 18 Exceptions, Escalations, and Prohibited Conduct When the standard path fails, pause and ask rather than improvise a risky commitment. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Escalate immediately  Account ownership dispute  Prospect complaint or opt-out concern  Request for price, contract, guarantee, or legal commitment outside authority  Data source or privacy concern  Suspected fraud, impersonation, or conflict of interest  Security incident or lost device, SIM, password, or file  Harassment, threat, discrimination, or retaliation concern  Material client dissatisfaction or reputational risk Prohibited conduct  False identity, fake appointment, fake pipeline, or fabricated evidence  Bribery, kickbacks, undisclosed referral payments, or improper gifts  Unauthorized subcontracting or sharing of company access  Contacting excluded or suppressed accounts  Moving Engage Lynk opportunities outside the approved relationship  Manipulating records to claim attribution  Publishing company, client, or prospect information without permission  Continuing activity after suspension or termination

chunks.title: BD Partners SOP
chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | BD PARTNERS SOP Internal Use | Engage Lynk | 21 SECTION 19 Security, Confidentiality, and Data Protection Partners receive minimum necessary access and remain accountable for secure handling. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Required controls  Use assigned accounts and multi-factor authentication where available.  Do not share passwords, one-time codes, API keys, SIMs, or licensed seats.  Do not move files to personal email, drives, or unapproved messaging apps.  Do not place confidential or personal data into unapproved AI tools.  Use only approved prospect data for the approved purpose.  Report suspected breaches or unauthorized access immediately.  Return or delete protected information when instructed and legally permitted. Legal review Cross-border outreach, high-volume processing, telemarketing, electronic messaging, and personal-data use must be reviewed against current applicable law and client instructions before launch.

chunks.text: ENGAGE LYNK | BD PARTNERS SOP Internal Use | Engage Lynk | 22 SECTION 20 Suspension, Corrective Action, and Termination Protect prospects and the company while applying a fair, documented process. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Condition Possible response Minor process gap Coaching, correction, or retraining Repeated data-quality failure Opportunity hold or reduced access Unauthorized claim or promise Immediate review, correction, and possible suspension Security or confidentiality concern Immediate containment and access restriction Fraud, harassment, bribery, or deliberate deception Immediate suspension and termination review Inactivity or strategic misfit Territory release, non-renewal, or orderly exit Offboarding procedure 25.Freeze or close opportunity registration as instructed. 26.Transfer all active records, meetings, and commitments. 27.Return devices, SIMs, files, and branded materials. 28.Disable accounts and rotate shared credentials. 29.Confirm treatment of protected pipeline under the agreement. 30.Reconfirm confidentiality, non-circumvention, and data-return obligations. 31.Complete final statement and dispute window where applicable.
